'''Alison Ramage''' is a British [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[numerical analysis|numerical analyst]] specialising in [[Preconditioner|preconditioning]] methods for [[numerical linear algebra]], and their applications to the numerical solution of [[partial differential equations]]. She is a reader in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Strathclyde]].{{r|strath}}

==Education and career==
Ramage is a graduate of the [[University of St Andrews]].{{r|strath}} She completed her PhD in 1991 at the [[University of Bristol]]. Her dissertation, ''Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Methods for Galerkin Finite Element Equations'', was supervised by Andrew Wathen, and involved preconditioners for the [[Galerkin method]].{{r|strath|mg}}

She is a member of the board of trustees of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].{{r|trustee}}

She currently serves as Chair of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) Board of Trustees.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sven Leyffer and Alison Ramage Started SIAM Leadership Positions January 1 |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/sven-leyffer-and-alison-ramage-started-siam-leadership-positions-january-1 |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=SIAM News |date=6 January 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Research==
Ramage's thesis involved preconditioners for the [[Galerkin method]], and applications to the numerical solution of [[partial differential equations]] in [[computational fluid dynamics]], including those for [[incompressible flow]] and [[advection–diffusion equation]]s. Subsequently, she has applied her research to other areas including [[geotechnical engineering]], [[financial mathematics]], modeling [[liquid crystal]]s, [[weather forecasting]], and [[sensor network]]s.{{r|strath}}
